### Authentication Setup

Every tool call requires you to be logged in to your Mermaid account. Signing up is free — the Basic tier costs nothing. There are two ways to authenticate:

#### Option 1: OAuth Login (recommended)

If your MCP client supports OAuth discovery, no manual token setup is required. The first time you call a tool, a browser window opens asking you to log in to your Mermaid account. Once you log in, your client stays authenticated automatically — no token needs to be added to your config.

Just use the plain, header-free configuration examples above.

#### Option 2: Manual Token-Based Authentication (still supported)

  1. Get Your Token: Visit your Mermaid account settings and generate an API token
  2. Add to Configuration: Include the token in the `Authorization` header as shown in the examples above
  3. Replace Placeholder: Change `YOUR_MERMAID_TOKEN_HERE` with your actual token

If the token is missing or invalid, and OAuth login hasn’t completed, every tool call is rejected.

Connect to your Mermaid account (authentication)

Without authentication, the MCP Server can validate syntax and render diagrams. To also save diagrams to your Mermaid account, list your existing projects, or update saved diagrams, you'll need to authenticate with an API token.

  1. Generate an API token. Sign in to your Mermaid account and go to your account settings. Scroll to the Secure tokens for plugins section and click Create new token. A new token will appear with a default name. Click the eye icon to reveal the token value, then click the copy icon to copy it. You can rename the token by editing the name field (e.g., to "MCP Server").
  2. Add the token to your MCP configuration. Include it in the Authorization header as shown in the setup examples. Replace `YOUR_MERMAID_TOKEN_HERE` with the token you just copied.
  3. Restart your AI client. The server will now have access to your Mermaid account.

For the full list of authenticated operations (listing projects, creating diagrams, updating diagrams, etc.), see the MCP Server documentation.

## FAQ

Have questions about Mermaid API? These should help.

Contact sales

What is Mermaid API, and how is it different from Mermaid?

Mermaid is the open-source language and library that turns text into diagrams. Mermaid API is a hosted service that runs Mermaid for you: your program sends diagram code over HTTP and gets back a validation result, an image, or new diagram code.

Do I need a Mermaid subscription?

No. Any Mermaid account works, including a free one, and every account gets a monthly allowance of API credits. Paid plans include a bigger allowance.

How does pricing work?

Each call costs a set number of API credits. Your monthly allowance is spent first, then any credits you have bought. Costs are published in the docs, and a free endpoint tells your program what it has left. For high volume, contact sales.

Which diagram types and output formats are supported?

Every diagram type Mermaid supports (see the docs). Images come as SVG, PNG or PDF.

What happens to my diagram code?

We don't store it. Rendered images are cached for up to a day so a repeated request is fast, and you can turn caching off per request. Our usage records hold counts and sizes, never your diagrams.

Can I pin a Mermaid version?

Yes. Each call can name the Mermaid version it should use, so your output stays the same until you choose to upgrade.

Is it production-ready?

Mermaid API is in open beta. You can build on it; breaking changes are announced in advance in the changelog, and there is no uptime guarantee yet.

Where are the docs?

At api.mermaid.ai/v1/docs, with examples, an OpenAPI document and an llms.txt for agents.

Breaking changes are announced, not versioned: each is listed in the changelog at the end of this guide with its date and what a caller must do. Every response carries `x-mermaid-api-phase: beta` until general availability. Do not build a production dependency on it yet.

## Authentication

Every `/v1` call except the reference endpoints needs an API key: `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Keys are created in the console by any Mermaid Chart user, shown once at creation, and have no expiry by default. A key is `<prefix>.<secret>`, the prefix `mmd_` and twelve hex digits; the prefix appears in listings, the secret is stored only as a hash. A refused key is 401 with `www-authenticate: Bearer` and one of `ERR_KEY_MISSING`, `ERR_KEY_UNKNOWN`, `ERR_KEY_REVOKED`, `ERR_KEY_EXPIRED`: fix the key, do not retry. `ERR_KEY_OWNER_DELETED` means Mermaid Chart no longer knows the key's owner: the key works again once it does, within 5 minutes. The examples below take the key from `$MERMAID_API_KEY`.

## Validate

`POST /v1/validate`, a valid diagram:
    
    `curl -s "https://api.mermaid.ai/v1/validate" \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer $MERMAID_API_KEY" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{"code": "flowchart TD\n  A[Start] --> B[Done]"}'
    `
    
    `{ "valid": true, "diagramType": "flowchart-v2" }
    `

## Your key and your files

  * Your key stays out of the chat. The agent passes the credentials file or `MERMAID_API_KEY` straight to `curl`, and the skill tells it never to print or read them. Don’t paste the key into the chat yourself.
  * The key lives outside your projects, so it can’t be committed by accident.
  * The agent creates only the files you ask for, and removes its scratch files.
  * A failed render never overwrites an existing file.

## Troubleshooting

The agent says no key is set up, but you saved one. Check the file name. The skill reads `~/.config/mermaid-api/credentials` and nothing else in that folder; a file named `.env` is ignored. Run the setup command again, or rename your file. If `MERMAID_API_KEY` is set, it is used instead of the file.

401 `ERR_KEY_UNKNOWN`. The key wasn’t copied whole. Run the setup command again with the whole key, or create a new one in the console.

401 `ERR_KEY_REVOKED` or `ERR_KEY_EXPIRED`. The key no longer works. Create a new one in the console. An organisation admin can restore a revoked organisation key.

402 `ERR_LIMIT_BALANCE`. Your credits are spent. The agent stops and tells you. Ask it for your balance to see when your monthly allowance resets.

429 `ERR_LIMIT_BURST`. Too many calls in one minute. The agent waits as long as the API asks, then retries once. An uncertain create/share result needs reconciliation before another write; see the stored-diagram workflow.

Anything else. The agent looks the error up and explains it. When you report a problem to Mermaid, include the `x-request-id` the agent gives you.

## Reference

### Credentials file

`~/.config/mermaid-api/credentials` holds one line, readable only by you (mode 600):
    
    `Authorization: Bearer mmd_<12 hex characters>.<secret>`

### Environment variables

Variable  | Effect
--- | ---
`MERMAID_API_KEY`  | The bare key, without `Authorization: Bearer`. Takes precedence over the credentials file.
`MERMAID_API_URL`  | Points the skill at another Mermaid API deployment. Defaults to `https://api.mermaid.ai`.
